text.p: The following are the main stories in Slovenia's Tuesday morning newspapers:
- Slovenian truck driver Bostjan Mrak, who was arrested last Friday by British Police in an attempt to smuggle 200 kilos of heroine, had his first hearing on Monday.

- An Italian citizen and a person of unknown identity tried to rob a bank in the coastal town Lucija on Monday, but the Italian who tried to escape with the robbed money was caught by a plainclothes policeman off duty.
- Slovenian President Milan Kucan on Monday nominated new ambassadors to Turkey, France and to the Slovenian mission at the UN and other international organisations in Geneva.

- Every day some 50 Bosnian refugees leave Slovenia to return to Bosnia, authorities said. Last year some 10,000 refugees returned to their homes, some 5,100 Bosnians are expected to stay on in Slovenia this year.

- The number of births in Slovenia in 1996 fell by one percent compared to the previous year. The number of Slovenians aged 100 years rose to 47 people of a total population of 1,986,448, the Statistical Office of Slovenia reported.

- July trading volume on the Ljubljana bourse was at a record high. Securities worth 16.8 billion tolars ($98.5 million) were sold in July, this was 13.7 percent more than in February, the month with the previous highest turnover.
- Slovenian health resorts contributed 34.1 percent to tourism figures for the first half year.
